title: The first Pullman berth and seniority in Cab's band
summary: New men got upper berths; he spent five minutes figuring out how to climb into his on his first night.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So that was a great experience for me to join that band, plus the fact, the first time I ever rode a Pullman in my life -- I often think about it and I have to laugh, because there was a thing in the band of seniority, so all the guys who had seniority rode in the lower berth and the new guys had to get the upper ones.

Well, my first night, I forgot where we were going now, but my first night, I stood in the aisle and just took off my clothes and put my pajamas on, and I'm standing there figuring how I'm gonna get up in this berth, and nobody told me nothing -- and I didn't want them to know I was dumb and didn't know how to get up in the Pullman, so I stood there for at least about 5 minutes trying to figure out how to get up in that berth.
But after about a week, I could make it in two, one, two, and I was up there.
Panama, if anybody was to listen to the history of your life and listen to mine, would find that

they're exactly the same.

The exact same thing happened to me in 1936 in Cab Calloway's band, and it happened to you in '46 -- 10 years later, exactly the same thing. The very first Pullman I ever got in and the whole seniority thing, standing around waiting for everything, which is beautiful, we all loved that, it was a beautiful school.
The Cab Calloway School of Musical Knowledge, it should be called.
